title: External Agent Registry Entry
description: One external agent CLI, described as data. Metadata only: argv construction, event parsing and failure classification live in a codec module per agent, because the CLIs differ structurally rather than parametrically (decisions.md D-06). Adding an agent is one entry here plus one codec module.

id.description: Runtime id used in the dispatch `runtime.agent` field.

label.description: Display name for the TUI sidebar and modal.

binary.description: Executable name resolved on PATH. keryx never reads this agent's credential store; presence of the binary says nothing about whether the operator is logged in.

detect.description: Argv appended to the binary to prove it exists and report a version. Must not spend subscription quota.

versionPattern.description: Regular expression with one capture group extracting a version string from the detect output.

knownGoodRange.description: Version range this agent's codec fixtures were recorded against. A version outside the range produces a recorded warning on the run; it never blocks.

sandboxModes.description: Sandbox levels the CLI itself supports. This is agent capability, NOT the keryx release gate: what keryx has implemented is a separate runtime refusal, so 'this agent cannot do that' and 'keryx does not do that yet' stay distinguishable reasons. A dispatch naming a mode absent here is rejected fail-closed.

streamingInput.description: Whether the CLI accepts operator messages mid-run. When false, messages are held and delivered through the resume path instead; the supervision layer branches on this field rather than on the agent id.

resumable.description: Whether a killed session can be resumed by its id, which is what makes `force` cost a process restart rather than the accumulated work.

reportsCost.description: Whether the CLI reports a monetary cost keryx can surface. A missing figure is displayed as missing, never as zero.

budgetFlag.description: Whether the CLI accepts a native budget ceiling keryx can forward, so exhaustion is a clean BudgetExhausted rather than an unbounded run.

notes.description: Free-text operator-facing note, shown in the modal's Meta tab.

examples.label: Codex
examples.notes: Reports token usage on turn.completed but no monetary cost. Operator messages are delivered by resuming the session.

examples.label: Claude
examples.notes: Accepts streaming input, a native budget ceiling, and a keryx-assigned session id.
